$comment: Tool ids (KitObjectModel OM9; KHP A44, A46, A47, A48): a type's `toolId` names the read-only field holding the id the kit's tools give its objects, and the object model answers and takes that id. Run in order on one new document of `schema` by kition-kdm (tests/tool_ids.rs) and @kition/kdm (test/tool-ids.test.ts), against a target standing in for a kit: after each transaction it numbers every object of a type with a `toolId` that has no number, one more than the highest of its type under the same holder (the type's parent), in type then id order, and its one command `echo` answers its parameters. A step answers `result` or fails with `error`, message included, and changes nothing; `diff` is the draft comparison of the states before and after the step. `Pin` and `Flag` are numbered apart but share the empty prefix, so their ids collide and they answer their object ids. `schemaErrors` gives a type another `toolId` (and `fields`, when given) and the error parsing the schema answers.

steps.$comment: Objects created in a batch are named by `$name` or their object id within it, and answered with the tool ids the kit gave them; a type without `toolId` keeps object ids.
Targets, references, and loads take tool ids, a parent's included; a reference loads as the tool id it names; an object id still names its object.

A created object is addressed later in its batch by `$name`; a command's parameters get its tool id; after a command the next run names it by its tool id; the draft comparison names objects by tool ids.
An unknown tool id is not-found, listing the ids of its domain when they are few.

schemaErrors.message: schema: type `Frame`: `toolId` names `name`, which is not `readOnly`: only the kit writes an object's tool id
schema: type `Frame`: `toolId` names `link`, which is not an integer or a string
schema: type `Frame`: `toolId` prefix `frame.`: a prefix holds ASCII letters, digits, `_`, `-`, `:`, and `/` only
schema: type `Frame`: `toolId` prefix `1:`: a prefix starts with a letter
schema: type `Cell`: `toolId` names parent `Doc`, which declares no `toolId`
schema: type `Cell`: `toolId` names parent `Pin`, which has no list, tree, or ref field of `Cell`
schema: type `Frame`: `toolId` parent `Frame` leads back to `Frame`: parents form no cycle
